args.objective: Visit the hub index at 127.0.0.1:36017/hub-index, then for each of the three regional hubs read its dispatch day from its own page and its defect rate from the independent audit office page it links to, then report all three dispatch days, all three defect rates, and the hub with the lowest defect rate.
args.headline: Collect dispatch days and defect rates for three regional hubs

args.excerpt: Hub Aurora dispatches standard fixture widget orders on Tuesday.
args.observation: Hub Aurora's own page states its dispatch day is Tuesday.

args.excerpt: Hub Aurora returned a defect rate of 4.1% over the audited quarter.
args.observation: Independent audit office reports hub Aurora's defect rate is 4.1% for the audited quarter.

args.excerpt: Hub Borealis dispatches standard fixture widget orders on Friday.
args.observation: Hub Borealis's own page states its dispatch day is Friday.

args.excerpt: Hub Borealis returned a defect rate of 0.9% over the audited quarter.
args.observation: Independent audit office reports hub Borealis's defect rate is 0.9% for the audited quarter — the lowest of the three hubs.

args.excerpt: Hub Cascade dispatches standard fixture widget orders on Wednesday.
args.observation: Hub Cascade's own page states its dispatch day is Wednesday.

args.excerpt: Hub Cascade returned a defect rate of 2.7% over the audited quarter.
args.observation: Independent audit office reports hub Cascade's defect rate is 2.7% for the audited quarter.

metrics.answerText:
Collected each hub's dispatch day from its own page and its defect rate from the independent audit office page each hub links to:

| Hub | Dispatch day | Defect rate (audited quarter) |
|---|---|---|
| Aurora | Tuesday | 4.1% |
| Borealis | Friday | **0.9%** |
| Cascade | Wednesday | 2.7% |

**Borealis has the lowest defect rate (0.9%)** — well below Cascade (2.7%) and Aurora (4.1%).

Sources: [hub index](http://127.0.0.1:36017/hub-index) → [Aurora](http://127.0.0.1:36017/hub-aurora) + [audit](http://127.0.0.2:41915/audit-aurora), [Borealis](http://127.0.0.1:36017/hub-borealis) + [audit](http://127.0.0.2:41915/audit-borealis), [Cascade](http://127.0.0.1:36017/hub-cascade) + [audit](http://127.0.0.2:41915/audit-cascade).

scenarios.command: three competing explanations for the Q3 fixture widget recall are filed at http://127.0.0.1:36017/recall-brief. for each explanation, read its dossier and the independent lab report it links, then tell me which explanation the lab evidence supports, with the measurement it rests on, and say what ruled out each of the other two

args.objective: Read the Q3 fixture widget recall brief and its three explanation dossiers plus each linked independent lab report; determine which explanation the lab evidence supports, the key measurement behind it, and what ruled out the other two.
args.headline: Compare three recall explanations against their independent lab reports

args.observation: Lab report: ceramic coating cure — cure times were within tolerance on every recalled batch; theory NOT supported by lab evidence.
args.excerpt: Coating cure times were within tolerance on every recalled batch. This theory is NOT supported.
Bearing seats on every recalled batch were machined 0.4 mm undersize. This theory is SUPPORTED.
args.observation: Lab report: bearing seat machining — bearing seats on every recalled batch machined 0.4 mm undersize; theory SUPPORTED (the 0.4 mm undersize measurement is the deciding evidence).

args.excerpt: Packaging matched spec on every recalled batch. This theory is NOT supported.
args.observation: Lab report: packaging compression — packaging matched spec on every recalled batch; theory NOT supported by lab evidence.

args.subject: Q3 fixture widget recall cause: bearing seat machining (seats 0.4 mm undersize) is the lab-supported explanation
args.detail: Of the three theories on the recall brief, only the independent lab report on bearing seat machining supports its theory; coating cure and packaging compression are ruled out.

metrics.answerText:
I read the recall brief's three dossiers plus each one's independent lab report:

**Supported: bearing seat machining** — The lab report states: "Bearing seats on every recalled batch were machined 0.4 mm undersize. This theory is SUPPORTED." The decisive measurement is the **0.4 mm undersize** bearing-seat dimension, found consistently across every recalled batch ([lab report](http://127.0.0.2:41915/lab-bearing)).

**Ruled out: ceramic coating cure** — "Coating cure times were within tolerance on every recalled batch. This theory is NOT supported." There was no cure-time deviation to explain the failure ([lab report](http://127.0.0.2:41915/lab-coating)).

**Ruled out: packaging compression** — "Packaging matched spec on every recalled batch. This theory is NOT supported." The packaging was never undersized, so transit compression can't be the cause ([lab report](http://127.0.0.2:41915/lab-packaging)).

Each theory's dossier itself states no verdict; all three verdicts come from the independent lab reports the dossiers link.
